what: ServiceNow sells software that automates workflows inside large organisations. It began with IT service desks and now runs HR, customer service, security and AI-driven processes on one platform.
customers: Large enterprises and governments; most of its revenue comes from a few thousand big accounts.
money: annual platform subscriptions, renewed and expanded over time
moat: Once its platform runs the processes a company depends on daily, replacing it means rebuilding workflows across many departments, so renewal rates are very high.
risks: The shares trade at a high multiple, so any slowdown in growth is punished
Large enterprise deals can slip between quarters
Stock-based compensation is large relative to reported profit
Microsoft bundles competing capability into existing agreements
opportunities: Revenue has grown above 20% a year with subscription renewal rates among the best in software
AI agents give it a new product line to sell into accounts it already serves
Expanding beyond IT into HR, finance and customer service multiplies the addressable spend per client
watch: Current remaining performance obligations, which show contracted revenue ahead, and net new annual contract value.
